purpose: Durable, source-indexed provider model/access knowledge artifact for future OpenClaw model capability routing. This artifact does not implement the router.

claims.text: OpenClaw must keep provider model capability separate from access mode, subscription entitlement, API billing health, and local runtime availability.
Winship's current policy preference is to use subscription-backed CLI/app lanes before API-key billing or credit pools.

The Gemini API route has provider config present but is blocked by a 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED prepayment-credit condition, so capability routing must not confuse model suitability with provider credit health.

provider_vs_access_mode_vs_capability.model_capability_layer: GPT-5.5/GPT-5.4 API families, GPT Image, Realtime, transcription, video/Sora, Agents SDK, Responses API.
provider_vs_access_mode_vs_capability.access_mode_layer: Codex CLI/app/web are coding-agent access modes; ChatGPT app/web remains manual-only for OpenClaw until a supported bridge is proven.
provider_vs_access_mode_vs_capability.billing_layer: API pricing/caching/batch/flex are API billing controls; Codex subscription entitlement is a separate access-mode fact.

provider_vs_access_mode_vs_capability.model_capability_layer: Gemini 3.x text/multimodal models, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Live/TTS/audio models, Nano Banana/Imagen/Veo/Lyria creative models, embeddings, Deep Research, Computer Use, and Antigravity Agent.
provider_vs_access_mode_vs_capability.access_mode_layer: Gemini CLI and Antigravity CLI are installed locally but subscription/auth/billing mode is not proven; Gemini API is not the preferred default route.
provider_vs_access_mode_vs_capability.billing_layer: Gemini API provider health is currently blocked by RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and must remain separate from model capability.

provider_vs_access_mode_vs_capability.model_capability_layer: Claude Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5, plus documented Fable 5 and related Claude Code access surfaces.
provider_vs_access_mode_vs_capability.access_mode_layer: Claude CLI is installed locally, but subscription/auth/billing mode is not proven by the current audit.
provider_vs_access_mode_vs_capability.billing_layer: Claude API pricing/context facts are distinct from Claude Code subscription or console/provider authentication.

provider_vs_access_mode_vs_capability.model_capability_layer: Installed local models are suited first for private classification, redaction, and bounded local proof-to-response tests, not automatically for high-accuracy advisory routing.
provider_vs_access_mode_vs_capability.access_mode_layer: Ollama is a local runtime, not subscription-backed access.
provider_vs_access_mode_vs_capability.billing_layer: No API billing is required for local inventory, but invocation still requires an OpenClaw boundary receipt.

claims.text: OpenAI documents GPT-5.5 as the newest frontier model for complex reasoning and coding/professional work.
OpenAI documents GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 Pro, GPT-5.4 mini, and GPT-5.4 nano as GPT-5.4-family options with lower-cost/lower-latency tiers below the frontier model.

OpenAI positions the Responses API and Agents SDK around model calls with tools, state, guardrails, approvals, and structured outputs, while Structured Outputs constrains model text to a supplied JSON Schema.
OpenAI documents separate Realtime/audio paths for voice agents, live translation, transcription, and text-to-speech; file transcription is handled through speech-to-text models.
OpenAI documents GPT Image generation/editing and Sora video-generation APIs as specialized creative media surfaces.
OpenAI documents prompt caching, Batch API, cost optimization, and evals as tools for lowering cost, managing latency, and measuring quality during model upgrades.
OpenAI documents Codex CLI, app, and web/cloud as coding-agent access surfaces included with ChatGPT plans; in OpenClaw these are worker/access modes, not Cassandra's chat brain.
OpenAI documents Codex app computer use, but OpenClaw should keep computer-use/desktop-control disabled by default behind Guardian and explicit operator approval.

router_implications: Treat GPT-5.5 as an API model capability candidate for hardest reasoning only after an approved API-billing route exists.
Treat GPT-5.4 mini/nano as lower-cost code/subagent candidates only when access mode and billing boundary are approved.
Use Codex CLI as the likely first subscription-backed code-worker lane after an auth/subscription proof; do not promote it to live chat brain.
Keep image, video, realtime, transcription, computer-use, hosted tools, and creative media disabled by default.

claims.text: Google documents Gemini 3.5 Flash as a sustained frontier-level, faster/lower-cost model for real-world and agentic tasks, with multimodal input, structured outputs, function calling, code execution, grounding, caching, and large context.
Google documents Gemini 3.1 Flash Live Preview for low-latency audio-to-audio dialogue and Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS Preview for low-latency speech generation.
Google documents Nano Banana image models, Imagen 4, Veo 3.1 video models, Lyria 3 music models, and Lyria RealTime as creative media capabilities.

Google documents Deep Research, Computer Use, and Antigravity Agent as agent/tool surfaces; Antigravity is a managed agent powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash and can run code, use files, and browse in a hosted sandbox.
Google documents Gemini embeddings for semantic search/classification/RAG and publishes a deprecation/lifecycle page for model shutdown schedules.
OpenClaw should not route new Gemini work through Gemini 2.x candidates except as explicitly excluded legacy references.

router_implications: Gemini 3.5 Flash is the best documented Google candidate for fast advisory/form-fill, but current OpenClaw API health is blocked by provider credits and CLI subscription mode is unproven.
Gemini CLI and Antigravity CLI should remain worker package candidates, not live conversation providers, until auth/billing and no-tools/no-file boundaries are proven.
Deep Research, Computer Use, Antigravity Agent, Veo, Imagen/Nano Banana, and Lyria are disabled-by-default capability classes requiring Guardian/operator gates and separate cost controls.
Lyria belongs in a Niles/creative-media branch only after explicit creative media approval; it is not a general business response model.

claims.text: Anthropic documents Claude Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, and Haiku 4.5, with Opus positioned for advanced reasoning/coding/creative tasks, Sonnet as balance, and Haiku as the fastest low-cost tier.

Anthropic documents 1M context windows for Claude Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Claude Fable 5, and Claude Mythos 5 on specified surfaces; other models can remain at 200k depending on platform.
Anthropic documents effort tuning for recent Opus and Sonnet models and recommends considering effort as a cost/latency lever before switching models.

Anthropic documents Claude Code surfaces including Terminal CLI and notes that most surfaces require a Claude subscription or Anthropic Console account; CLI reference documents noninteractive print, piped content, model selection, tools controls, and JSON output options.
Local Claude CLI help exposed model aliases including fable, opus, and sonnet; Haiku was not observed in local help and should not be claimed as locally selectable without a future auth/model probe.

router_implications: Claude CLI can become a review/deep-reasoning worker lane only after subscription/auth mode and no-tools boundaries are proven.
Claude API model power should not imply OpenClaw tool or business authority.
Fable/Opus/Sonnet naming should be treated as provider-specific aliases requiring current model-config verification.

claims.text: The current local audit found Ollama installed with local models, including qwen3:8b-q4_K_M and other local candidates; no local model invocation was performed by the audit.
Local/Ollama models are the preferred class for private classification/redaction and bounded local pilots when an invocation boundary exists.

router_implications: Use local models for private redaction/classification first; do not infer high-quality deep reasoning without eval evidence.
Local presence does not equal invocation permission; every pilot still needs approval, redaction, verifier, and receipt boundaries.

claims.text: OpenClaw's latest provider access catalog found Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI, Claude CLI, and Ollama installed, but did not prove subscription/auth backing for the cloud CLIs.
The Worker Run Manager/Codex package lifecycle supports bounded package states, allowed worker kinds, result ingestion, and authority boundaries that keep model output from mutating runtime directly.
The Assignment Loop contract frames work as bounded assignments with goals, sources, standards, permission boundaries, proof requirements, receipts, Watch Desk refs, and stop conditions.
The Model Work Package Router currently builds advisory-only packages and deterministic model-class decisions without calling models or granting execution authority.
Watch Desk aggregates read models into proof-backed display items and remains display-only, not an approval or execution surface.

router_implications: Router inputs must include task class, data sensitivity, access mode, provider health, subscription/auth proof, budget posture, tool/desktop risk, and required receipts.
Model capability can recommend a lane but cannot grant tool, desktop, browser, email, Coupa, ledger, workbook, PDF, paid, or push authority.
Codex should route as a code-worker/access mode; Cassandra's live chat brain should remain deterministic/proof-to-response until a separately approved conversational LM path exists.
API routes remain fallback-only until explicitly configured and approved because subscription-backed usage is the preferred cost posture.
Creative media, computer use, managed agents, and tool-use models require disabled-by-default feature flags, Guardian gates, and per-run receipts.
subscription_backed_access_implications: Prove each CLI's auth/subscription/billing mode through a separate safe status probe before treating it as subscription-backed.
Do not infer subscription backing from installation or local help output.
ChatGPT app/web is manual-only until a supported bridge exists; do not browser-scrape or GUI-automate it.
Codex CLI is the first likely subscription-backed implementation worker candidate once auth/subscription proof exists.
Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI, and Claude CLI are candidate worker lanes but require auth/billing-mode and no-tools/no-file boundary receipts before dispatch.
cost_latency_accuracy_doctrine: Use deterministic local logic when it can answer from proof without a model.
Use local/Ollama for private redaction/classification where quality risk is acceptable and verifier coverage exists.
Use subscription-backed CLI workers before API billing when the task is code/review/advisory and proof can be bounded.
Use API models only for capability gaps that subscription/local access cannot satisfy and only after cost/provider health/approval receipts exist.
Prefer cheaper/faster model tiers for high-volume, low-risk work only after evals prove acceptable accuracy.
evals_accuracy_target_doctrine: Every router lane needs fixtures before live use: schema compliance, unsupported-claim refusal, protected-action refusal, source citation behavior, and fallback behavior.
Provider/model upgrades require regression evals on OpenClaw proof-to-response, package review, form-fill, code-worker, and stale-context tasks.
Do not lower verifier or Guardian thresholds to make a model pass.
Capture latency/cost and accuracy separately; a faster or cheaper model is not acceptable if it increases unsupported claims or stale-context leakage.

what_not_to_build: Do not build a new approval system; use Guardian/HITL.
Do not build a new dashboard; feed Watch Desk/read models.
Do not start Hermes to watch catalogs in this task.
Do not route private finance proof to external providers by default.
Do not make Gemini API credits the main route while provider health is blocked.
Do not make ChatGPT app/web an automated lane without a supported bridge.
Do not enable computer-use, managed agents, creative media, or browser/file tools by default.

next_build_tasks.goal: Prove auth/subscription/billing mode for Codex, Gemini, Antigravity, and Claude CLIs without printing credentials or invoking generation.
Define router inputs/outputs using this dossier, provider access catalog, assignment loop, Guardian gates, and Worker Run Manager.
Create bounded, non-business smoke packages for CLI worker candidates after auth mode is proven.
Build offline eval fixtures for proof-to-response, code review, form-fill, stale-context, protected-action, and unsupported-claim behavior.
